purpose: Cromolyn is used to help prevent asthma attacks, allergic nasal symptoms like sneezing and runny nose, and certain digestive problems caused by food allergies. It works best when used regularly before you are exposed to things that trigger your symptoms. It is not a rescue medication, so it won't help once symptoms have already started.
how_it_works: Think of mast cells as little alarm bells in your body that go off when you encounter something you are allergic to, releasing chemicals that cause your symptoms. Cromolyn works by coating and stabilizing those mast cells so they don't release those irritating chemicals in the first place. It basically helps keep the alarm from going off before trouble starts.
common_side_effects: The nasal spray may cause mild stinging, sneezing, or a temporary burning sensation in your nose. The inhaled form can occasionally cause throat irritation or a mild cough. The oral form may cause nausea, diarrhea, or stomach upset in some people.
warnings: Cromolyn is a preventive medication only — never use it to treat a sudden asthma attack or severe allergic reaction. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using it. Do not stop taking it suddenly without checking with your healthcare provider, as your symptoms may return. Let your doctor know if your symptoms get worse or do not improve after a few weeks of regular use.
typical_dosing: For the nasal spray, the usual dose is one spray in each nostril three to four times a day. For inhaled asthma prevention, it is typically used four times a day. The oral liquid for food allergies is usually taken four times a day, 30 minutes before meals. Your doctor will give you the exact dose that is right for your situation.
